name: broader-development-2026-11-14-v2
spanConvention: half-open Unicode code-point indices into exact unnormalised text

denominators.uniqueFactMetricRule: Score BD01-BD12 once each. Exclude BDC04 repeated BD07 from unique-fact accuracy. Report control admission/privacy separately; BDC04 is an eligible-span isolation control, not a negative-admission case.

provenance.purpose: Open development and tuning. This is not a blind or held-out evaluation.
provenance.authorImplementationAccess: No implementation or diffs inspected. Only project AGENTS.md and public docs/plan.md were read; eligibility/evidence sections used for labels.
provenance.sealedDataAccess: No sealed or original heldout contents inspected or changed. Coincidental overlap with unknown sealed cases is possible and was not checked.
provenance.selectionPolicy: Twelve diverse stable low-stakes factual topics selected before pipeline execution. No engine or provider performance used for selection. Wording clarified during source review, before any pipeline run.
wordingRefinements: Magna Carta: replaced draft sealing-location assertion with first-issued year, because source scholarship warns against assuming one original sealing ceremony.
UNESCO: replaced draft organization-establishment wording with Constitution adoption date, distinguishing entry into force.
provenance.research: Connected Exa search/fetch only; no project API keys, no project pipeline calls.

sourceRequests.note: Counts describe research requests, not 80 unique reviewed or qualifying sources; repeated results are not independent evidence.

provenance.review: Independent source/label review required before use; author checks are not independent review.
provenance.latency: Not measured. Research retrieval time is not pipeline latency.
provenance.generalization: Small deliberately balanced development set; no population or broad accuracy claim supported.

cases.label: BD01
cases.text: The Great Fire of London occurred in 1666.

acceptedTexts: The Great Fire of London occurred in 1666.

allowedPublic: The Great Fire of London occurred in 1666.

publicSpans.text: The Great Fire of London occurred in 1666.

cases.groundTruthRationale: The Great Fire of London took place in September 1666; only its year is tested.
cases.scope: calendar year of the historical London fire

cases.label: BD02
cases.text: Magna Carta was first issued in 1216.

acceptedTexts: Magna Carta was first issued in 1216.

allowedPublic: Magna Carta was first issued in 1216.

publicSpans.text: Magna Carta was first issued in 1216.

cases.groundTruthRationale: Its first issue dates to June 1215. The 1216 version was a later reissue.
cases.scope: first issue, not a later reissue; no exact sealing-location assertion

cases.label: BD03
cases.text: Mount Kilimanjaro is located in Tanzania.

acceptedTexts: Mount Kilimanjaro is located in Tanzania.

allowedPublic: Mount Kilimanjaro is located in Tanzania.

publicSpans.text: Mount Kilimanjaro is located in Tanzania.

cases.groundTruthRationale: The maintained volcano country record and encyclopedia place Kilimanjaro in Tanzania.
cases.scope: named mountain's country; no elevation/eruption-status claim

cases.label: BD04
cases.groundTruthRationale: Lake Baikal is in Siberia, Russia, not Africa.
cases.scope: named lake's continent/location; no depth ranking or volume claim

cases.label: BD05
cases.text: In the SI definition of the second, the unperturbed ground-state hyperfine transition frequency of the caesium-133 atom is fixed at 9,192,631,770 Hz.

acceptedTexts: In the SI definition of the second, the unperturbed ground-state hyperfine transition frequency of the caesium-133 atom is fixed at 9,192,631,770 Hz.

allowedPublic: In the SI definition of the second, the unperturbed ground-state hyperfine transition frequency of the caesium-133 atom is fixed at 9,192,631,770 Hz.

publicSpans.text: In the SI definition of the second, the unperturbed ground-state hyperfine transition frequency of the caesium-133 atom is fixed at 9,192,631,770 Hz.

cases.groundTruthRationale: BIPM fixes this exact transition frequency to 9 192 631 770 Hz in defining the second.
cases.scope: SI normative definition as checked 2026-11-14; unperturbed ground state, hyperfine transition, caesium-133, exact fixed value, unit Hz

cases.label: BD06
cases.text: The chemical symbol for gold is Ag.

acceptedTexts: The chemical symbol for gold is Ag.

allowedPublic: The chemical symbol for gold is Ag.

publicSpans.text: The chemical symbol for gold is Ag.

cases.groundTruthRationale: Gold's symbol is Au. The tested symbol Ag is not gold's symbol.
cases.scope: standard chemical element symbol, not an alloy/brand abbreviation

cases.label: BD07
cases.text: The Panama Canal opened to world trade in 1914.

acceptedTexts: The Panama Canal opened to world trade in 1914.

allowedPublic: The Panama Canal opened to world trade in 1914.

publicSpans.text: The Panama Canal opened to world trade in 1914.

cases.groundTruthRationale: The Panama Canal Authority gives 15 August 1914 as opening to world trade.
cases.scope: opening to world trade, not construction start, earlier test passage, expansion or transfer

cases.label: BD08
cases.text: The first modern Olympic Games were held in Paris in 1896.

acceptedTexts: The first modern Olympic Games were held in Paris in 1896.

allowedPublic: The first modern Olympic Games were held in Paris in 1896.

publicSpans.text: The first modern Olympic Games were held in Paris in 1896.

cases.groundTruthRationale: The first modern Games were held in Athens in 1896.
cases.scope: first modern Olympic Games; neither ancient Games nor founding of IOC in Paris

cases.label: BD09
cases.text: UNESCO's Constitution was adopted in London on 16 November 1945.

acceptedTexts: UNESCO's Constitution was adopted in London on 16 November 1945.

allowedPublic: UNESCO's Constitution was adopted in London on 16 November 1945.

publicSpans.text: UNESCO's Constitution was adopted in London on 16 November 1945.

cases.groundTruthRationale: The legal text explicitly gives adoption in London on 16 November 1945; entry into force was a different event on 4 November 1946.
cases.scope: adoption of Constitution, place London, exact date; no member/signatory-count assertion

cases.label: BD10
cases.text: The Smithsonian Institution was created by a British royal charter in 1846.

acceptedTexts: The Smithsonian Institution was created by a British royal charter in 1846.

allowedPublic: The Smithsonian Institution was created by a British royal charter in 1846.

publicSpans.text: The Smithsonian Institution was created by a British royal charter in 1846.

cases.groundTruthRationale: It was established by an act of the US Congress approved on 10 August 1846, not a British royal charter.
cases.scope: legal establishment mechanism in 1846; founder's British nationality is separate

cases.label: BD11
cases.text: Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen received the first Nobel Prize in Physics in 1901.

acceptedTexts: Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen received the first Nobel Prize in Physics in 1901.

allowedPublic: Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen received the first Nobel Prize in Physics in 1901.

publicSpans.text: Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen received the first Nobel Prize in Physics in 1901.

cases.groundTruthRationale: The Nobel award record identifies Röntgen as 1901 recipient; independent biography identifies it as the first Physics Nobel.
cases.scope: first Physics Nobel recipient and year; not a claim about first prize in any category or discovery date

cases.label: BD12
cases.text: The Great Barrier Reef lies off the west coast of Australia.

acceptedTexts: The Great Barrier Reef lies off the west coast of Australia.

allowedPublic: The Great Barrier Reef lies off the west coast of Australia.

publicSpans.text: The Great Barrier Reef lies off the west coast of Australia.

cases.groundTruthRationale: It lies off Australia's northeastern coast in the Coral Sea.
cases.scope: named Great Barrier Reef's location; no current ecological-status assertion

cases.label: BDC01
cases.text: I misplaced my blue notebook on the train yesterday.

privateSpans.text: I misplaced my blue notebook on the train yesterday.

cases.groundTruthRationale: A synthetic private lived event. Do not search it or issue a public truth verdict.
cases.scope: Synthetic control; truth labels do not apply.

cases.label: BDC02
cases.text: Handwritten postcards are more charming than digital messages.
cases.groundTruthRationale: A pure aesthetic preference with no separable factual proposition.
cases.scope: Synthetic control; truth labels do not apply.

cases.label: BDC03
cases.groundTruthRationale: Unresolved treaty referent and unfinished time/place clause. An explicit manual request must receive clarification (terminal needs_confirmation). Initial bounded waiting may occur; no public search or truth verdict is permitted.
cases.scope: Synthetic control; truth labels do not apply.

cases.label: BDC04
cases.text: My rent is €980 a month. The Panama Canal opened to world trade in 1914.

acceptedTexts: The Panama Canal opened to world trade in 1914.

allowedPublic: The Panama Canal opened to world trade in 1914.

publicSpans.text: The Panama Canal opened to world trade in 1914.

cases.groundTruthRationale: Synthetic rent statement must stay out of every public query. Only the exact independent second sentence is eligible; it reuses BD07 and adds no unique fact.
cases.scope: Mixed control tests isolation/privacy; truth applies only to public clause, never to private rent.
